newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up in slow holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up in slow holiday trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly higher Thursday in a very quiet session.

"Most of us are on vacation and the rest are here just in case something happens. There was no fixed trend, although a strong performance by some ADRs probably tipped the balance towards the close," a dealer said.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 12.42 points, or 0.38 percent, at 3,310.89. Volume was wafer thin at 31.5 million shares traded.

On Wall Street, ADRs listed by market heavyweights Telmex and Televisa ended up 3/4 and 1/4, respectively, at 32-1/2 and 25-3/4. Their peso equivalents gained 16 centavos (2 cents) and 50 centavos (6 cents), respectively, to 12.72 pesos ($1.62) and 101.00 pesos ($12.86).

Trading also was dulled by announcements of forthcoming rises in controlled prices for milk and tortillas. These staples weighed heavily in the inflation index, and could thus fuel inflation and interest rates, traders said.
On the broad market, 89 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered losers 41 to 23.

Traders noted that the gainers and losers lists were dominated by infrequently traded stocks and small trades. Financial stock Confia headed the leaders, up 1 peso (13 cents) to 4 pesos (51 cents), but after a trade of just 16,000 shares, the first time it had traded since Nov 21.
Situr, the tourist arm of the debt-ridden Sidek group, headed the losers, after falling 2 centavos (1 cent) to 38 centavos (5 cents).
Traders saw more dull sessions for the remainder of the year.
"We might get some demand for window-dressing on Monday or Tuesday, but otherwise we'll still be right in the doldrums," a trader said.
